figures.title: This paper in the 13 components, against the field
figures.subtitle: Each box: what this paper does, then common practice across all sensors and how many ledger papers share it.
figures.caption: Verdicts compare the paper's choice for each component with common practice across 8,995 ledger entries on any sensor (silent speech, brain-to-text, lip reading).

choice: Spoken-speech EEG of the same words and participants
M01.field: Overt-speech training data for a silent-mode decoder
M01.note: Same design as M04; spoken data argued to be easier to acquire (§III.A).

M02.note: Class labels only; no auxiliary training target.

choice: Within-subject; all or 10 spoken trials per class; no fine-tuning
M03.note: 10-trial model averages 28.0% vs 26.8% with all trials (Table I, untested); fine-tuning left to future work.

choice: Imagined speech decoded by a spoken-trained model
M04.field: Overt-trained decoder applied to silent or covert speech without retraining

M05.note: Dataset of earlier studies by the same group (§II.B).

M06.note: No preprocessing or classifier settings reported.

M08.note: No speech output despite the vocalization claim (§IV).

choice: Instructed imagery labels; session arrangement not stated
M11.note: Authors concede imagined content cannot be verified (§I).

choice: Random 90/10 10-fold CV baseline; one Kruskal-Wallis test over 3 conditions; no chance level
M12.note: Omnibus p = 0.0983 read as "comparable"; no pairwise or equivalence test.

choice: Offline; application to impaired users proposed
M13.note: No online use, latency or user study.
